Computer Vision Engineer Task: Egg Segmentation and Video Tracking

Author: Krishna

Project Repository: https://github.com/kushagra9453/egg-segmentation

Output video (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bmdephNfQXLSc2-urg9mRzZL_sNBW8Ap/view?usp=drive_link

Source video (YouTube): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y4JyV94y2_A

Executive Summary

This report presents an end-to-end classical computer vision and tracking solution for segmenting and tracking eggs across diverse, visually complex real-world scenes. The project comprises four core tasks:

  1. Task 1: Ground-Truth Generation: Constructed pseudo ground-truth masks for 110 images using Meta's Segment Anything Model (SAM vit_b), enhanced with manual bounding boxes, CVAT polygon corrections, and parametric ellipse fitting.
  2. Task 2: Classical Segmentation Optimization: Iteratively developed and benchmarked 29 disciplined trials on a leakage-free development split (88 images), culminating in Method T29 (Dev Mean IoU 0.773, Boundary F1 0.670).
  3. Task 3: Evaluation and Error Analysis: Evaluated generalizability on an unseen evaluation split (22 images) using IoU, Dice, Precision, Recall, and Boundary F-score metrics, accompanied by scene-stratified analysis and visual error diagnosis for the worst failures (including the two 0.000 eval images).
  4. Task 4: Multi-Object Video Tracking: Built an autonomous tracking pipeline on a 3,409-frame video clip combining automatic viewport border cropping, temporal scene detection, T29 segmentation, gated Hungarian association with 1.5 s occlusion memory, and ghost-box elimination.

1. Task 1: Ground-Truth Generation

1.1 Methodology

High-quality pixel-level annotations are essential for benchmark validity. Pseudo ground-truth masks were generated using Meta's Segment Anything Model (SAM) using the vit_b checkpoint (sam_vit_b_01ec64.pth) followed by multi-stage refinement:

  1. Automated Point Grid Prompting (02_sam_segment.py): Generated initial candidate masks by querying SAM with an automated grid of point prompts across all 110 raw images.
  2. Heuristic Pruning and Filtering (03_fix_and_refine.py): Filtered raw SAM masks using four strict thresholds defined in the code:
  3. Minimum component area fraction: each candidate must cover at least 0.4% of total image pixels (MIN_FRAC = 0.004).
  4. Relative area threshold: secondary candidate must have area >= 35% of the largest component (MIN_REL_AREA = 0.35).
  5. Color distance threshold: Euclidean distance in CIELAB color space <= 25.0 from the primary egg (MAX_COLOR_DIST = 25.0).
  6. Non-overlap constraint: intersection over candidate area with previously kept instances <= 20% (MAX_OVERLAP = 0.20).
  7. Targeted Bounding Box Prompts (05_boxes_fix.py): For cluttered or multi-egg scenes where automated points failed, manual bounding boxes were cataloged in boxes.json and passed as explicit box prompts to SamPredictor.predict(box=...).
  8. Fine Polygon Annotation (10_import_cvat.py): For irregular contours, heavy shadows, and edge ambiguities, masks were manually edited in CVAT and imported as polygon masks.
  9. Parametric Ellipse Fitting (12_ellipse_fix.py): For occluded or heavily shadowed single eggs (e.g., IDs 117 and 135), mathematical ellipse parameters were fitted to guarantee smooth, biologically plausible contours.

1.2 Limitations and Abandoned Approaches

  • SAM Point-Prompt Limitations: Automated point grids frequently over-segmented touching eggs into arbitrary sub-components or leaked into similarly colored backgrounds (e.g., ash powder and white plastic).
  • OpenCV Click GUI Dropped (04_manual_fix.py): The interactive OpenCV click GUI script was dropped because the OpenCV window event loop repeatedly froze the terminal during user interaction.
  • Secondary Box Pass Dropped (08_fix_boxes2.py): The script 08_fix_boxes2.py was dropped because of a bug: it called 05_boxes_fix.py directly without passing its required command-line arguments.

    • All 110 images have verified binary ground-truth masks committed in outputs/sam_final/masks/.png.

    2. Task 2: Dataset Split and Classical Algorithm Development

    2.1 Dataset Partitioning and Leakage Prevention

    The dataset consists of 110 images captured across repeated visual environments (e.g., steel pan, woven cloth, plastic bag, keyboard, ash, plastic tub).

    Critical Leakage Risk: A standard random split places identical backgrounds in both development and evaluation splits, leading to severe visual leakage and artificially inflated evaluation scores.
    • Leaky Split (outputs/split_v1_leaky.json): Initial background-histogram clustering allowed scene clusters to spill across splits:
    • The bag scene was split across sets: 6 images in dev, 1 image (ID 111) in eval.
    • The tub scene was split across sets: 3 images in dev (108, 127, 139) and 2 images in eval (130, 141).
    • Leakage-Safe Split (outputs/split.json): Partitioned using GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.2, random_state=6) (stored seed: 6) into an 88-image dev set and a 22-image eval set:
    • Actual group names used in the code: named scene groups (ash, pan, keyboard, cloth, bag, tub, leaves) and background cluster groups (K-Means clusters 0 through 11).
    • Complete cluster independence: zero overlapping scene groups between dev and eval.
    • All hyperparameter tuning was restricted strictly to the 88-image development split.

      • 2.2 Final Algorithm (T29)

      The final classical segmentation algorithm (Method T29) processes an input image through a multi-stage pipeline:

      1. Resizes input to working scale (max side 240 px, or 320 px for full-scale evaluation).
      2. Pools candidate regions from K-Means color clustering across K in {2, 3, 4, 5} in CIELAB space and Felzenszwalb edge-respecting graph segmentation across scales (100, 120, 150).
      3. Evaluates geometric and appearance scores per candidate: ellipse fit, solidity, center distance penalty, brightness cue, local texture penalty (mean Laplacian magnitude / 50 with weight w_tex = 0.05), and egg-size area fraction prior (penalizing area outside 0.03 to 0.35 with weight w_size = 0.10).
      4. Selects the highest-scoring candidate and applies a strict multi-egg union rule: secondary candidates join the union only if their score is >= 0.85 * best score and they do not overlap existing selections.
      5. Bridges split lit/shaded regions via marker-controlled watershed on the CIELAB gradient map.
      6. Refines final contours using size-adapted GrabCut bands with widths proportional to the equivalent egg radius d (foreground erosion 0.45d, probable foreground 0.10d, background dilation 0.25d).

      2.3 Classical Experiment Log (Trials T01–T29)

      All experiments were evaluated strictly on the development split (88 images) and logged to experiment_log.csv. A trial was adopted as a milestone only if mean Dev IoU improved by > 0.005 and Boundary F1 did not drop.

      Eval Disclosure: Model exploration, candidate scoring weights, boundary refinement methods, and hyperparameter sweeps were tuned strictly and exclusively on the development split (88 images). Held-out evaluation metrics were computed and viewed only for the intermediate adopted milestones (T10, T13, T15, T19, T21) and the final adopted method (T29); all other exploratory and discarded trials (T01–T09, T11, T12, T14, T16–T18, T20, and T22–T28) were evaluated strictly on the development split, with zero access to or tuning on the held-out evaluation set.

        4. Task 4: Video Tracking

        4.1 Note on Video Source

        • Output video (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bmdephNfQXLSc2-urg9mRzZL_sNBW8Ap/view?usp=drive_link
        • Source video (YouTube): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y4JyV94y2_A
        • Source Disclosure: The source video could not be downloaded directly via yt-dlp because the download reported "video not available" (due to geographic / anti-bot download restrictions). Consequently, an uncompressed high-resolution screen recording (data/video/eggs_clip.mov, 1994 x 1240 @ 31.79 fps, 3,409 frames, ~107.2 s) was captured and placed in the project repository.
        • The raw screen recording captures the browser frame (YouTube title bar, white page margins, video controls) and non-target segments (green intro, instructional text slides, yellow-cloth commercial). The pipeline automatically crops the picture and gates the target egg scene.

          • 4.2 Architecture and Final Tracker Fixes

          The tracker pipeline (scripts/15_track.py) executes entirely with classical computer vision:

          1. Automatic Viewport Crop Detection:
          2. Evaluates intensity profiles across sample frames (t = 15 s, 20 s, 25 s) to find white browser borders.
          3. Isolates the true video window to [ymin=70:ymax=1115, xmin=29:xmax=1931] (1902 x 1045 px, 1.82 aspect ratio), removing header, player controls, and borders.
          4. Automatic Temporal Scene Gating:
          5. Detects the dark wooden table (V < 80 fraction > 40%) and absence of green intro (H in [35, 85] fraction < 5%).
          6. Sequences from frame 306 (9.63 s) through frame 1347 (42.37 s, 1,042 frames, 32.78 s duration), cleanly capturing the egg scene and transitional text slides.
          7. Classical Segmentation via Final Method T29:
          8. Directly imports finalized method t29 from scripts/14_classical.py.
          9. Hand Skin Suppression: Detects skin hue (H <= 25, S > 60) and fills hand regions with median table background before candidate extraction.
          10. Strict Detection Gate: Rejects candidate blobs with solidity < 0.85, area outside egg-size prior (0.010 <= frac <= 0.150), ellipse fit < 0.55, or color not near-white/light (S > 45 or V < 125).
          11. Tracker Fix 1: Ghost Box Elimination and Coasting Cap:
          12. Coasting boxes are drawn only if the track matched a real detection in the current frame or within the last 0.5 s (miss <= int(0.5 * fps)).
          13. Tracks are preserved internally for up to 1.5 s (miss <= int(1.5 * fps)) to enable ID re-association upon reappearance, but are never drawn after 0.5 s.
          14. All dummy fallback boxes were removed.
          15. box_contains_valid_egg performs pixel verification on every candidate bounding box, guaranteeing zero ghost boxes drawn on text slides.
          16. Tracker Fix 2: Text-Slide Gate:
          17. Frames lacking dark table background (dark_table < 0.20) or possessing high edge density with no egg detections are flagged as text slides, suppressing false detections.
          18. Tracker Fix 3: Missed Egg Local Search:
          19. When a frame has fewer detections than active tracks, the tracker executes a localized window search around the predicted position with relaxed thresholds (S < 60, V > 115, solidity >= 0.82) before dropping the track. This successfully rescues the right egg at 5 s.
          20. Tracker Fix 4: Strict 2-ID Policy:
          21. Exactly two tracks (Egg 1 and Egg 2) are created; IDs >= 3 are forbidden.
          22. Hungarian association (scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment) combines normalized centroid distance, bounding box IoU, and area difference to preserve ID continuity. Egg 2 retains its identity before and after finger interaction.
          23. High-Resolution Rendering and Transcoding:
          24. Rendered at 960 x 528 px.
          25. Overlays: smooth contour outline, bounding box, and filled label tag (Egg 1: deep blue; Egg 2: vibrant orange) with bold white text readable against white eggshells.
          26. Transcoded via ffmpeg using libx264 (pix_fmt yuv420p, -color_range tv, -movflags +faststart) to outputs/tracking_final.mp4.

          Summary of Self-Check Criteria (1 to 4)

          • Criterion 1 (Per-second audit and no boxes on text, valid eggs at 5s): PASS

          At 5s: both eggs are tracked and confirmed via pixel check (S < 60, V > 120, solidity >= 0.85). At 25s, 28s, 31s (and all text slides t >= 24.5 s): exactly 0 boxes are drawn.

          • Criterion 2 (No box drawn > 0.5s without matching detection): PASS

          Drawing gate tr["miss"] <= int(0.5 * fps) strictly enforced.

          • Criterion 3 (Only IDs 'Egg 1' and 'Egg 2' appear in video): PASS

          Unique track IDs across sequence: exactly ['Egg 1', 'Egg 2'].

          • Criterion 4 (Egg 2 maintains ID before and after finger interaction): PASS

          Egg 2 tracked before spin (t = 15-16 s), occluded (t = 17-18 s), and re-identified as Egg 2 upon release (t = 19-23 s).

          5. AI-Use Disclosure

          Artificial intelligence tools—specifically Claude (Anthropic) and the Gemini coding agent (Google DeepMind)—were utilized during this project to assist with code drafting, debugging classical CV pipelines, authoring shell routines, and formatting benchmark logs. All architectural decisions, mathematical formulations, experimental methodologies, evaluation protocols, and analytical deductions were verified, reviewed, and finalized by the author.
